[verification_turn] I don't have any information about your company's standards—I'm not connected to your internal documentation, team conversations, or systems. So I can't tell you what your specific company requires.

To actually answer your question, you'd want to check:

- **Internal documentation** (architecture guidelines, API standards, an internal wiki)
- **Whoever mentioned this to you**—go back and ask them which standards they meant, since they clearly had something specific in mind
- **Existing services** in your codebase to see what's already in use

That said, here are protocols commonly relevant when integrating with legacy systems, so you have a vocabulary to ask better questions:

- **REST/HTTP** — modern default, but worth confirming the legacy side supports it
- **SOAP** — very common in older enterprise systems; if legacy systems were built 10-20 years ago, this is a real possibility
- **gRPC** — efficient, but unlikely on the legacy side unless recently modernized
- **Message queues** (AMQP/RabbitMQ, JMS, Kafka, IBM MQ) — IBM MQ in particular shows up a lot in older enterprise/financial environments
- **FTP/SFTP** — for batch file transfers, still surprisingly common in legacy workflows
- **TCP sockets / fixed-length or delimited formats** — some genuinely old systems use custom binary or flat-file protocols

The legacy systems usually constrain your choices more than the new service does—you often have to meet them where they are.

My honest recommendation: don't guess on this. The cost of picking the wrong protocol set is high (rework, integration failures), and the answer genuinely lives in your org. Ask your team lead or architect: *"Which protocols do our standards require, and what do the specific legacy systems I'm integrating with actually support?"*
